newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Rightist Aleman claims victory in Nicaragua vote.
newsitem.headline: Rightist Aleman claims victory in Nicaragua vote.

text.p: Right-wing populist Arnoldo Aleman claimed victory on Monday in Nicaragua's presidential elections, preaching reconciliation to a torn nation as new results continued to give him a strong lead.

With 6.96 percent of the vote counted, Nicaragua's election authorities said Aleman had won 48.68 percent of the vote, against 39.58 percent for his main rival Daniel Ortega, the former revolutionary leader of the 1979-1990 Sandinista government.
At a rally at his campaign headquarters, Aleman made a victory speech despite appeals from the Sandinistas to avoid "triumphalist" messages until more votes were counted.
"From today, I invite everyone from the other political parties -- from the one in second place to the lowest placed -- to unite forces. Nicaragua needs all of us to leave the past behind," he said.
He said he expected to achieve at least 50 percent of the vote, above the 45 percent needed to avoid a run-off against Ortega.
Aleman campaigned on a fierce anti-Sandinista ticket, playing on fears that they would return Nicaragua to its violent past.
